passage:
A city placed sensors at busy crossings to count pedestrians. The data showed that far more people crossed near a hospital than planners had expected.
The city widened the sidewalk and added more crossing time at the light.
A student asked why planners had not simply watched the street earlier. The engineer admitted that observation should have happened sooner. Sensors helped, but they were not a replacement for paying attention.
The project improved safety, but it also taught humility.
Cities are full of people solving their daily problems by walking. Good planning begins by noticing those movements before someone gets hurt.
